title: Plunger, coffee-can and glass mutes
summary: He has long used plungers, coffee cans, milk cans and a glass over the bell to vary the trumpet sound.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: The glass, when did you start using a glass?

Well, I just, well, Mr. Bill, I just, sometime I, I've been doing that, you know, sometime I used to use that rubber spludger. Yeah, plunger. I used to use that long time ago. Then sometime I used to take a coffee can, you know what I mean? I'd make a, take a coffee can. I'd take that coffee can and I'd cut, I'd cut on the top of it so it could fit right on top of my bell. Oh yeah. You know what I mean? And sometimes take a tin can, a little tin can, you know what I mean? Small tin, milk can, you know? Yeah. And blow it in a glass and anything, you know what I mean? And blow it like that, you know? That's some nice sounds. Yeah, a long time, you know, I've been fooling on with that.
